name: Macro Regime 2EMA Pro (VIX-DXY vote + EMA50/200)
author: ALCIVOOO
summary: Trades crypto in the direction of the EMA50/EMA200 trend only when VIX and DXY macro states vote risk-on (long) or risk-off (short).
long_entry: (close > ema(close, 50)) & (close > ema(close, 200)) & (vix < sma(vix, n)) & (dxy < ema(dxy, m))
short_entry: (close < ema(close, 50)) & (close < ema(close, 200)) & (vix > sma(vix, n)) & (dxy > ema(dxy, m))
notes: Source does not publish numeric VIX/DXY thresholds; risk-on approximated as VIX below its SMA and DXY below its EMA. USDT dominance vote, trailing stop, break-even and partial TP omitted.

name: Global Liquidity + BTC divergence
author: Nomi_chen
summary: Normalised Fed net liquidity minus normalised BTC; positive (liquidity ahead of price) is a bullish catch-up setup, negative is overheated.
notes: Original uses weekly data and 0-1 min-max normalisation; approximated with daily z-scores over 26/52 weeks. Optional 10-week liquidity lead mentioned by author not included.

name: Global M2 YoY leads BTC by ~10 weeks
author: Matt (Look Into Bitcoin)
summary: BTC trails global M2 year-on-year growth by about 10 weeks (best fit 56-60 days); accelerating M2 growth precedes BTC breakouts.
notes: Needs global M2 (multi-central-bank money supply in USD), not in vocabulary; netliq is US-only and a different measure.

name: Faber 10-month SMA on S&P 500 as BTC filter
author: Mebane Faber
summary: Classic tactical timing: hold the risk asset while the index month-end close is above its 10-month SMA, else cash; here the S&P 500 signal gates BTC.
notes: Faber's 10-month monthly SMA approximated by a ~210-trading-day daily SMA checked only at month end. Applying the equity signal to BTC is the catalogue's cross-asset adaptation; Faber tested equities/asset classes.

name: BTC month-end 200-day SMA switch
author: Seeking Alpha contributor
summary: Faber-style rule on BTC itself: on the last day of each month buy if BTC is above its 200-day SMA, sell if below; claimed profitable with smaller drawdowns.
notes: Faithful to the stated rule; BTC trades 7 days a week so the 200-day SMA spans fewer calendar months than on equities.

name: Coutts DXY drop >2.5% -> long BTC 90 days
author: Jamie Coutts (Real Vision), via NewsBTC
summary: On the 8 occasions since 2013 that DXY fell more than 2.5% (short window), BTC was higher 90 days later every time.
notes: Measurement window of the DXY decline not stated precisely; m in bars assumed. Exit approximates a 90-day hold: flat once no qualifying DXY drop has occurred within the last 90 bars.

name: Zweig breadth thrust (taker-flow approximation)
author: Martin Zweig (described by BabyPips)
summary: Bull-market start signal when the 10-day EMA of advancing/total issues moves from below 0.40 to above 0.615 within 10 days.
notes: Rough approximation: NYSE advance/decline breadth replaced by BTC taker-buy share, thresholds rescaled because taker_ratio sits near 0.5. Zweig gives no exit (one-off bullish trigger); exit on taker EMA below 0.5 is an assumption.

name: Net liquidity fair value premium (Anderson / dharmatech)
author: dharmatech, after Max Anderson
summary: SPX fair value = (Fed balance sheet - TGA - RRP)/1.1 - 1625; short when SPX is >350 points above fair value, cover when the premium falls below 150.
notes: Absolute 1.1/1625 calibration depends on netliq units, replaced by a z-score spread between SPX and netliq; used as a risk-off gate for BTC (out when equities are rich versus liquidity). Original trades SPX short.

name: Arthur Hayes USD liquidity index trend
author: Arthur Hayes (index), TradingView chart publisher
summary: Fed balance sheet minus RRP minus TGA; Hayes argues BTC's path follows this USD liquidity index - be long when it is rising.
notes: Hayes gives direction, not a rule; 'rising' approximated as netliq above its n-day SMA.

name: Declining 2-year yield is bullish BTC
author: TradingView idea author
summary: Falling US 2-year yields weaken the dollar and push capital to risk assets such as BTC; rising 2y is a headwind.
notes: Idea is qualitative; 'declining' approximated as us2y below its n-day SMA. Author warns falling yields from recession fear can be bearish.

name: VIX >30 reversal / VIX <20 directional crypto filter
author: cryptohubble
summary: Use VIX for crypto: only take reversal (buy-the-fear) trades when VIX > 30 and directional trend trades when VIX < 20.
notes: Source gives only the VIX levels; the reversal trigger (BTC reclaiming a short EMA) and exit are assumptions to make it a complete rule.

name: Fed Net Liquidity Premium EMA cloud
author: armandogoldmanlaszlo (Golman Armi)
summary: Net liquidity (WALCL - TGA - RRP) with an EMA cloud: green expansion supports bullish risk-asset trends incl. BTC, red contraction warns of volatility/bear phases.
long_entry: (netliq > ema(netliq, n)) & (ema(netliq, n) > shift(ema(netliq, n), k))
long_exit: (netliq < ema(netliq, n)) & (ema(netliq, n) < shift(ema(netliq, n), k))
notes: Closed-source; EMA length unknown. Expansion approximated as netliq above a rising EMA. 'Hollow rally' divergence filter not included.

name: Newzage Fed Net Liquidity fair value + RSI
author: momentumX_capital, after Max Anderson
summary: SPX fair value from net liquidity (Fed balance sheet - TGA - RRP) combined with RSI overbought/oversold to time long and short entries.
notes: Original targets SPY; applied as BTC entry gate. Fair value replaced by z-score spread (netliq unit calibration unknown); RSI thresholds not published, 30/70 standard defaults assumed.

name: DXY Bias (EMA cross on DXY)
author: Intromoto
summary: Colours BTC/altcoin charts by DXY EMA-cross bias: bearish DXY cross = bullish crypto bias, bullish DXY cross = bearish bias.
notes: Invite-only script; EMA lengths not disclosed, common pairs assumed. Engulfing-candle 'R' markers omitted.

name: INDEX MA Filter (DXY above MA = bearish crypto)
author: Sharingtrade56
summary: Trend filter for crypto: DXY or USDT dominance above its moving average is bearish for crypto, below is bullish.
notes: MA type/length protected; SMA assumed. USDT.D, BTC.D and TOTAL variants need dominance/market-cap data not in vocabulary.

name: QQQ/NDX net liquidity fair value bands
author: dharmatech
summary: Nasdaq fair value bands from Net Liquidity (Fed - RRP - TGA); Nasdaq stretched above its liquidity value is a risk-off warning.
notes: Fair value regression and band offsets not shown on page; approximated with z-score spread NDX vs netliq and used as a BTC risk gate.

name: BTC down + VIX up shared-risk channel exit
author: Convex Research Desk (Ben Bleier)
summary: Crypto-only crashes rarely push VIX above 30; a multi-week stretch where BTC falls while VIX rises signals the equity shared-risk channel is engaging (deeper drawdowns).
notes: Article is a risk-monitoring note, not a strategy; turned into a risk-off filter using its VIX>25 stress threshold. HY spread (>400bp) and ETF-flow triggers not in vocabulary.

name: Risk-Off Ladder (VIX rank, 200d MA, 15% drawdown)
author: oridahari
summary: Three warnings (VIX in top 20% of its 1-year range, price below 200-day MA, price >15% below 1-year high): 0-1 warnings = 100% invested, 2-3 warnings = 0%.
long_entry: ~((((vix - lowest(vix, 365)) / (highest(vix, 365) - lowest(vix, 365)) >= 0.8) & (close < sma(close, 200))) | (((vix - lowest(vix, 365)) / (highest(vix, 365) - lowest(vix, 365)) >= 0.8) & (close < 0.85 * highest(close, 365))) | ((close < sma(close, 200)) & (close < 0.85 * highest(close, 365))))
long_exit: (((vix - lowest(vix, 365)) / (highest(vix, 365) - lowest(vix, 365)) >= 0.8) & (close < sma(close, 200))) | (((vix - lowest(vix, 365)) / (highest(vix, 365) - lowest(vix, 365)) >= 0.8) & (close < 0.85 * highest(close, 365))) | ((close < sma(close, 200)) & (close < 0.85 * highest(close, 365)))
notes: Built for QQQ/SPY; VIX percentile rank approximated by position in its 1-year range (365 daily bars). 70% SuperTrend re-entry tier and 10-bar rebalance delay omitted (binary 100/0).

name: Trend Safety Switch (SuperTrend + VIX/MA/drawdown warnings)
author: oridahari
summary: Long-only SuperTrend(10,3) with ADX(14)>=15 entry filter; goes to 0% when 2+ of: VIX 252-bar rank >= 80, close < 200 MA, drawdown from 1-year high > 15%.
long_entry: (supertrend_dir(10, 3) > 0) & (adx(14) >= 15) & ~((((vix - lowest(vix, 252)) / (highest(vix, 252) - lowest(vix, 252)) >= 0.8) & (close < sma(close, 200))) | (((vix - lowest(vix, 252)) / (highest(vix, 252) - lowest(vix, 252)) >= 0.8) & (close < 0.85 * highest(close, 365))) | ((close < sma(close, 200)) & (close < 0.85 * highest(close, 365))))
long_exit: (supertrend_dir(10, 3) < 0) | (((vix - lowest(vix, 252)) / (highest(vix, 252) - lowest(vix, 252)) >= 0.8) & (close < sma(close, 200))) | (((vix - lowest(vix, 252)) / (highest(vix, 252) - lowest(vix, 252)) >= 0.8) & (close < 0.85 * highest(close, 365))) | ((close < sma(close, 200)) & (close < 0.85 * highest(close, 365)))
notes: VIX rank approximated by range position. The 30% residual holding on SuperTrend down-flips in healthy markets is dropped (full exit). Assumes supertrend_dir > 0 means uptrend.

name: Panic Marker: buy the first VIX>=30 close after a calm stretch
author: Nambou_Signals
summary: Buy when VIX closes >= 30 after 60 calm sessions and hold ~3 months or ~1 year; on SPX 14 of 21 panics since 1990 were higher a year later.
notes: Calm defined as no VIX close >= 30 in the prior 60 bars (source's calm level not stated). Exit approximates fixed-horizon hold: flat h bars after the last VIX>=30 close. Tested by author on S&P 500, applied here to BTC.

name: DXY monthly return with 3-month lead (Steno)
author: tiagostrdvw (after Steno Research chart)
summary: 21-trading-day DXY return shifted forward 3 months leads BTC/crypto inversely: falling dollar three months ago = bullish crypto now.
notes: No explicit signal in source; sign of the lagged 21-day DXY change used. Script cites both ~10-week and 3-month leads, hence lead 50-70 bars.

name: BTC vs DXY and US02Y sentiment gauge
author: PresentTrading
summary: Rising DXY (safe-haven bid) and rising 2-year yield (tightening expectations) pressure BTC; both falling is a supportive backdrop.
notes: Script plots ratios without published thresholds; rising/falling approximated vs n-day SMA. Title says US10Y but description US02Y; us2y used.

name: Crypto/DXY scoring (DXY return z-score dump warning)
author: MXWLL-Capital-Trading
summary: Scores crypto strength versus DXY with effect-size and z-score statistics; a DXY strength spike through its upper line warns of a crypto dump.
notes: Formulas and lengths not published; approximated by z-score of daily DXY returns breaking a threshold (exit) and returning below it (re-entry). RS/RSMOM, Hedges' g, Cliff's delta, RRG views omitted.

name: Liquidity Regime Oscillator (netliq + DXY + credit + equity beta)
author: myhcael
summary: 0-100 oscillator from Fed assets, TGA, RRP, DXY, HYG/LQD credit spreads and SPHB/SPHQ equity risk appetite; above 50 = expansionary risk-on, below 50 = risk-off.
notes: Credit-spread ETFs (HYG/LQD) and high-beta/quality ETFs (SPHB/SPHQ) are not in vocabulary; weights and smoothing lengths unpublished.

name: Macro Risk On/Off Sentiment (9-input z-score composite)
author: ichimokucorner
summary: Weighted z-scores (lookback 30) of VIX, S&P 500, US10Y, gold, DXY, emerging markets, HY spreads, copper/gold and put/call; positive composite = risk-on.
notes: Six of nine inputs (10y yield, gold, EM, HY spreads, copper/gold, put/call) are outside the vocabulary; weights not stated.

name: RiskONess (tedtalksmacro risk-on/off composite)
author: Austimize, after tedtalksmacro
summary: Aggregates tedtalksmacro's global risk-on/off indicators into one score; higher = risk-on markets, lower = risk-off.
notes: Inputs not documented on page (cross-asset ratios beyond vocabulary); cannot be reconstructed.

name: Bull/Bear Market Regime (CBOE implied correlation + VIX)
author: SheepWoolos
summary: Risk-on/risk-off regime from CBOE implied correlation and VIX: green = low vol low risk bull, red = high vol bear.
notes: Needs CBOE implied correlation index (options data), not in vocabulary; thresholds unpublished.

name: Market Regime Index (trend across 32 markets)
author: QuantitativeAlpha
summary: Applies trend signals across 32 global markets and classifies the aggregate as risk-on or risk-off, alerting on regime changes.
notes: Requires 32 cross-asset series; only a handful are in vocabulary.

name: 42MACRO GRID macro regime (growth/inflation quadrant)
author: Celestial-Eye, after Darius Dale / 42 Macro
summary: Estimates GRID regime probabilities (goldilocks/reflation/inflation/deflation) from bond, index and ETF performance; risk assets favoured in goldilocks/reflation.
notes: Needs a basket of bond/factor ETFs and growth/inflation data not in vocabulary.

name: Copper/Gold ratio risk-appetite oscillator
author: RWCS_LTD
summary: Normalised copper/gold ratio as a fear-greed gauge: rising ratio = growth/risk appetite, falling = fear.
notes: Copper and gold prices not in vocabulary.

name: Global Net Liquidity (Fed+BoJ+PBoC+BoE+ECB - RRP - TGA)
author: dharmatech
summary: Sums five central-bank balance sheets in USD minus RRP and TGA as a global liquidity driver of risk assets.
notes: Needs non-US central-bank balance sheets and FX rates; vocabulary netliq is US-only.

name: M2 Global Liquidity Index with 78/108-day offset
author: TibixAi
summary: USD-weighted M2 of 5 or 13 economies shifted forward 78 or 108 days as a leading guide for BTC.
notes: Global M2 not in vocabulary.

name: Mannarino Market Risk Indicator (DXY x US10Y)
author: Emilio2014, after Gregory Mannarino
summary: MMRI = DXY x 10-year yield / 1.61; higher readings mean higher market risk (risk-off).
notes: Needs the 10-year yield; vocabulary has only us2y.

name: M2SL / DXY liquidity ratio for crypto
author: boy2004609
summary: US M2 divided by DXY as a dollar-liquidity gauge for crypto: rising ratio = more liquidity, weaker dollar.
notes: US M2 (M2SL) not in vocabulary.

name: MOVE vs VIX 1-year range position
author: Heard_Floor
summary: Bond-vol (MOVE) range position minus equity-vol (VIX) range position; bond stress leading equity vol flags risk-off.
notes: MOVE index not in vocabulary.

name: OECD M3 YoY >= 7% bubble trigger
author: Stephen Perrenod
summary: BTC follows a power law in OECD M3 (slope ~11.5, R2 0.86); M3 YoY growth peaks of ~7%+ preceded BTC bubbles by ~11 months.
notes: OECD M3 money supply not in vocabulary.

name: Global Macro Regime (30-market scoring)
author: QuantitativeAlpha
summary: Scores 30 global equity, bond, commodity and currency markets to set the macro regime and risk-asset allocation tilts, with a built-in backtester.
notes: Needs ~30 cross-asset series; vocabulary has only spx/ndx/dxy/vix/us2y.

name: Crypto Macro Heatmap (liquidity/leverage/breadth risk regime)
author: invincible3
summary: Normalises liquidity, leverage, breadth and risk-participation metrics to 0-100 and classifies crypto as risk-on, neutral or risk-off.
notes: Uses stablecoin, open-interest and crypto breadth data not in vocabulary; weights unpublished.

name: Hindenburg Omen breadth gate
author: Longtoonmaew
summary: NYSE-internals Hindenburg Omen (four conditions) sets a red risk-freeze; green when under 30% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 200-day.
notes: NYSE new highs/lows and % of stocks above 200-day are breadth data not in vocabulary.

name: Yield curve inversion/steepener regime
author: QuantAlgo
summary: Tracks 10Y-2Y and 10Y-3M spreads, inversion length and bull/bear steepener-flattener regimes as recession/risk-off signals.
notes: Needs 10-year and 3-month yields; vocabulary has only us2y.

name: Hayes: MOVE above 130 means money printing is coming
author: Arthur Hayes
summary: Hayes: when the MOVE bond-volatility index rises above 130 some form of Fed money printing follows; he adds BTC risk once the Fed supplies liquidity and BTC retests and holds support.
notes: MOVE index not in vocabulary; the liquidity gate is qualitative.

name: Silicon vs Satoshi: NDX-first breakout rotation (BTC leg)
author: Quantpedia
summary: Rotate QQQ -> BTC -> cash: hold QQQ if it closes above its prior w-day max, else BTC if it breaks out, else cash; Variant A 2019-25 CAGR ~40%, Sharpe 1.7, max DD -18%.
notes: Only the BTC sleeve is expressible: long BTC when BTC breaks out and NDX does not (NDX breakout means the strategy holds QQQ instead). BTC sampled at the US close in the source; here daily BTC bars with ndx forward-filled.

name: Dual momentum between gold (GLD) and bitcoin (IBIT)
author: Quantpedia
summary: Weekly: hold whichever of BTC or gold has the higher positive X-week return, else cash; 8-week version ~80% p.a., Sharpe 1.64; composite of 4/8/12 weeks Sharpe 1.47.
notes: Gold price not in vocabulary (needed for relative momentum).

name: Pre-holiday drift in bitcoin (US market holidays)
author: Quantpedia
summary: Equity pre-holiday anomaly transferred to BTC: buy BTC before US stock-market holidays and exit after; reported surprisingly profitable.
notes: Needs a US exchange holiday calendar; not in vocabulary.

name: Coppock curve (Trendex model) on BTC
author: E.S.C. Coppock (Barron's)
summary: Monthly WMA(10) of ROC(14)+ROC(11); buy when the curve is below zero and turns up from a trough. Originally a long-term equity-index bottom signal.
notes: Monthly lengths converted to daily bars (14m~426d, 11m~335d, 10m WMA~304d). Original has no sell rule; exit when the curve turns down above zero is an assumption. Needs ~2 years of warm-up.

name: Williams VIX Fix bottom finder on BTC (CM defaults)
author: ChrisMoody, after Larry Williams
summary: Synthetic VIX for any asset: WVF = (22-bar highest close - low)/highest close; WVF above its upper Bollinger band (20, 2) or above 85% of its 50-bar high flags capitulation bottoms.
long_entry: (((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100) >= bb_up(((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100), 20, 2)) | (((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100) >= 0.85 * highest(((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100), 50))
long_exit: ((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100) < sma(((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100), n)
notes: Entry uses the script's standard defaults (22, BB 20/2.0, lookback 50, 0.85). The indicator has no exit; exit when WVF drops back below its n-bar mean (fear normalised) is an assumption.

name: Market Fear Meter: fear-fading buy (VIX Fix rank)
author: oridahari
summary: 0-100 mood gauge: fear side ranks Williams VIX Fix over 252 bars, greed side ranks distance above the 50-bar average; FEAR FADING (leaving the fear zone) is the watch-for-a-buy moment, filtered by price above 200-bar MA or drawdown under 20%.
long_entry: (highest(((((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100) - lowest(((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100), 252)) / (highest(((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100), 252) - lowest(((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100), 252))), 5, 1) >= 0.8) & (((((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100) - lowest(((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100), 252)) / (highest(((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100), 252) - lowest(((highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) * 100), 252))) < 0.8) & ((close > sma(close, 200)) | (close > 0.8 * highest(close, 365)))
long_exit: ((close / sma(close, 50) - lowest(close / sma(close, 50), 252)) / (highest(close / sma(close, 50), 252) - lowest(close / sma(close, 50), 252))) >= 0.8
notes: Fear rank approximated by range position (not percentile); optional CBOE VIX blend omitted. No sell rule in source; exit on entering the greed zone (>=80) is an assumption.

name: Dual momentum: BTC vs S&P 500 vs T-bills
author: Gary Antonacci
summary: Monthly: pick the asset with the stronger 12-month return (relative momentum) but only if it beats T-bills (absolute momentum), else bonds/cash; here BTC is held when it beats both SPX and the short rate.
long_entry: (days_to_month_end == 0) & ((close / shift(close, n) - 1) * 100 > us2y) & (close / shift(close, n) > spx / shift(spx, m))
long_exit: (days_to_month_end == 0) & (((close / shift(close, n) - 1) * 100 < us2y) | (close / shift(close, n) < spx / shift(spx, m)))
notes: Antonacci's GEM compares equities and uses 12-month T-bill return; us2y (annual %) used as the T-bill proxy and SPX as the competing risk asset. n counts BTC calendar bars, m SPX-equivalent bars if spx is not forward-filled (use 365 if it is).

name: Market Sell-Off Gauge (BTC drop + stablecoin dominance + NDX + VIX + volume)
author: foosmoo
summary: Fuzzy-logic score of BTC % drop, USDT/USDC dominance rise, NDX weakness, VIX rise and high down-volume; entry circles when all conditions are met (BTC 4H/1D).
notes: Stablecoin dominance not in vocabulary; thresholds and weights are user inputs with no published defaults.

name: Gold/stocks ratio above 200-week MA = risk-off
author: capriole_charles (Charles Edwards)
summary: When the gold-to-stocks ratio is above its 200-week MA, gold has beaten equities for 20 years: a historic risk-off flag.
notes: Gold price not in vocabulary.

name: Halloween indicator / Sell in May applied to BTC
author: Bouman & Jacobsen (AER 2002)
summary: Equities earn most of their return November-April; sell at the start of May and buy back around Halloween. Found in 36 of 37 countries.
notes: Classic equity seasonal transferred to BTC as-is.

name: Santa Claus rally window on BTC
author: Yale Hirsch (Stock Trader's Almanac)
summary: Stocks tend to rise over the last 5 trading days of December and the first 2 trading days of January.
notes: Trading-day window approximated in calendar days for 24/7 BTC (last ~7 days of December + 1-2 January).

name: January barometer (S&P 500 January gates BTC for the year)
author: Yale Hirsch
summary: As goes January, so goes the year: a positive S&P 500 January predicts gains for the rest of the year.
notes: Cross-asset use: SPX January return (approx. 31 calendar bars, assumes forward-filled spx) decides whether BTC is held Feb-Dec.

name: January barometer on BTC itself
author: Yale Hirsch
summary: As goes January, so goes the year, applied to BTC's own January return.
notes: Own-asset variant of the Hirsch rule.

name: Dow Theory confirmation (BTC and ETH as the two averages)
author: Charles H. Dow / W.P. Hamilton / R. Rhea
summary: A primary bull trend is confirmed only when both averages (Industrials and Transports) make new highs; divergence warns of a turn.
notes: Rough analogue: BTC and ETH stand in for the Industrials and Transports; primary trend highs/lows via n-day breakouts. Dow's swing-structure rules are not expressible.

name: Multiple macro tailwinds checklist (liquidity, dollar, equities)
author: BIT Knowledge Hub
summary: Before taking a major BTC position check liquidity direction, dollar trend and equity trend: expanding liquidity + weakening dollar + strong equities = multiple tailwinds.
long_entry: (netliq > sma(netliq, n)) & (dxy < sma(dxy, n)) & (spx > sma(spx, n))
long_exit: ((netliq < sma(netliq, n)) & (dxy > sma(dxy, n))) | (spx < sma(spx, n))
notes: Qualitative checklist; trends approximated by n-day SMAs. The 'moderate correlation' leg needs a correlation function not in vocabulary.

name: G4 central-bank easing alignment
author: BIT Knowledge Hub
summary: Lean bullish crypto when global (G4: Fed, ECB, BoJ, PBoC) liquidity trends higher, maximally when all four ease together; defensive when all tighten. Check weekly, trade monthly/quarterly.
notes: ECB/BoJ/PBoC balance sheets not in vocabulary.

name: DXY below its 365-day MA is highly favourable for BTC
author: Darkfost (CryptoQuant), via Cointelegraph
summary: Periods with DXY below its yearly (365-day) moving average have historically been highly favourable for BTC; July 2025 saw the largest deviation below the 200-day in 21 years.
notes: Yearly MA length taken literally as 365 bars; if dxy is not forward-filled to 7 days use ~252.

name: Central Bank Liquidity Gap (liquidity growth minus S&P 500 growth)
author: HenriqueCentieiro
summary: Divergence = liquidity growth % - S&P 500 growth %; above +5% (liquidity outrunning stocks) has historically been a good buy zone; avoid new positions when deeply negative.
notes: Default liquidity is multi-country M2 (not in vocabulary); the script's optional Fed Net Liquidity mode is used. Growth lookback unpublished; 'deeply negative' exit threshold assumed. Applied to BTC rather than SPX.

name: M2 Liquidity Wave (global M2 leads BTC ~70 days)
author: bitcoin_briefs
summary: Projects a BTC 'probability cloud' from global M2 shifted 70-115 days (default 78); claims M2 leads BTC by about 70 days.
notes: Global M2 not in vocabulary.

name: Recession Warning Traffic Light (6 metrics)
author: BarefootJoey
summary: Gold/rhodium, SPX growth curves, 3m-10y inversion, GDP, M2 shrinkage and leading indicators combined into a recession probability; red = risk-off.
notes: Rhodium, gold, 10y/3m yields, GDP, M2 and LEI not in vocabulary.

name: BTC-equity correlation regime (post-2020 ~0.5)
author: CME Group OpenMarkets
summary: BTC-equity daily correlation averaged 0.2 (2014-2025) but rolling correlation jumped to ~0.5 from 2020; BTC trades as a high-beta (3-5x vol) equity in the high-correlation regime.
notes: Needs a rolling correlation function, not in vocabulary; article is descriptive (no trade rule).

name: BTC with VIX 21 risk threshold (QuantConnect)
author: QuantConnect community backtest
summary: BTC algorithm that uses a VIX high threshold of 21 as its regime level, with pyramid scaling into positions.
notes: Only the VIX=21 threshold is visible in the published code excerpt; direction (long below threshold, flat above) and the pyramiding are assumptions/omitted.

name: Art of the Dip: buy after a policy-driven VIX spike
author: GandalfTrades
summary: Satirical but explicit: go long when VIX jumps >=12% above yesterday's close with VIX >= 18; take half off when the spike fades, rest when VIX is back within 4% of prior close; 1.5% stop, 2.5% target.
notes: Original is intraday (5m, RTH) on index futures with a VIX9D>VIX filter and a 78-bar time stop; collapsed to daily bars on BTC, VIX9D filter and partial exit dropped.

name: Faber 10-month SMA timing on BTC (monthly closes)
author: MrOskama, after Mebane Faber
summary: Long when the monthly close is above the 10-month SMA, cash when it closes below; length adjustable (e.g. 12).
notes: 10/12 monthly closes approximated by a 304/365-day daily SMA evaluated at month end (BTC trades every day). Distinct from the 200-day month-end variant by lookback.

name: Nasdaq regime favourable for BTC
author: Ecoinometrics
summary: BTC is rejoining the risk-on complex: when the Nasdaq is in its historically favourable regime BTC returns are better, so BTC exposure follows the Nasdaq regime.
notes: Regime definition is paywalled; approximated as NDX above a rising n-day SMA (standard defaults).

name: TBL Liquidity Indicator (Treasury-market liquidity) red-dot signal
author: The Bitcoin Layer (Nik Bhatia, Augustine Carrasco)
summary: Proprietary Treasury-market liquidity index (auction demand, dealer positions, real yields, collateral capacity); turns in the index flag BTC/stock rallies, e.g. a 'red dot' confirmation at ~$76.6k in Sept 2026.
notes: Inputs are Treasury auction and dealer data, not in vocabulary; rule paywalled.

name: Payday anomaly (hold on the 16th) applied to BTC
author: Aixin Ma & William R. Pratt
summary: US equities earn abnormal returns on the 16th of the month (mid-month payday flows): buy the S&P 500 at the close of the 15th, sell at the close of the 16th.
notes: Equity payday-flow anomaly transferred to BTC; signals at the close of the 15th, trade held through the 16th.

name: Trading Fed rate decisions (cut/hike/pause criteria)
author: TanHef
summary: Backtests long/short trades triggered by Fed rate increases, decreases, double/aggressive moves or pauses (1971-present), with optional max trade duration.
notes: Needs the Fed funds target / decision calendar, not in vocabulary (us2y is only a proxy for expectations).

name: VIX term-structure regime engine (contango/backwardation)
author: QuantumAeon
summary: Classifies VIX1D-VIX6M curve shape (+VVIX) into backwardation (stress, high caution), front-end inversion, compression, healthy contango (normal bull) and expansion regimes.
notes: VIX term structure (VIX9D/VIX3M/VIX6M, VVIX) not in vocabulary; only spot vix available.

name: Post-FOMC rate decision performance
author: BBItsTime
summary: Shows how a security performed after past Fed rate decisions on the daily chart, to trade the post-FOMC drift.
notes: FOMC decision dates not in vocabulary.
